text.content: Meridian's canvas has grown significantly over three sprints. The Meridian Base Agent now handles knowledge retrieval, intent routing, live data lookup, retry logic, iteration, and human approval checkpoints, all in a single canvas.

text.content: As agent workflows grow in complexity, a new problem emerges. Logic that is useful in one flow frequently needs to be available in another. The engagement briefing logic built is a good example. It is useful as a standalone weekly tool and also as a capability the base agent should be able to invoke on demand. Rebuilding the same logic in every flow that needs it is not maintainable. When the briefing logic changes, every copy needs updating. When a bug is found, it needs fixing in multiple places. This is the problem that modular flow design solves.

text.content: What the Execute Flow Node does

rich_text.plain_text: What the Execute Flow Node does

text.content: The Execute Flow Node functions as a sub-workflow caller, promoting modular design and reusability of logic. It allows the current workflow to trigger a separate pre-existing workflow, pass an initial input to it, optionally override specific configurations of the target flow for that particular run, and receive its final output back into the calling workflow to continue processing.

rich_text.plain_text: The Execute Flow Node functions as a sub-workflow caller, promoting modular design and reusability of logic. It allows the current workflow to trigger a separate pre-existing workflow, pass an initial input to it, optionally override specific configurations of the target flow for that particular run, and receive its final output back into the calling workflow to continue processing.

text.content: In practical terms: One flow invokes another, waits for it to complete, and uses its output as if it were produced locally. The calling flow does not need to know how the sub-flow works internally, only what input it expects and what output it returns.

text.content: Known platform limitation

rich_text.plain_text: Known platform limitation

text.content: In complex canvases with multiple HTTP paths, the Execute Flow Node's Input field may auto-populate with variable references from other paths and revert on save. This is a known Flowise behaviour in certain canvas configurations. If you encounter this on your canvas, the full implementation is demonstrated in the live session using a clean canvas where this conflict does not occur. The configuration steps above are correct. The issue is specific to canvases with conflicting node ID bindings, not to the Execute Flow Node itself.

text.content: Takeaway:

rich_text.plain_text: Takeaway:

text.content: The Execute Flow Node converts isolated Agentflow v2 builds into reusable components. Logic built once can be invoked from any other flow without rebuilding. When the sub-flow changes, every caller benefits automatically. As Meridian's canvas grows, modular sub-flows keep individual components focused, independently testable, and maintainable without cascading changes across the entire build.
